elements.element: Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "Customer has no minimum purchase or volume commitment..." — the take-or-pay sentence (USD 2,000,000/year for three years, "without reduction or termination rights") is fully replaced, and the new wording is reinforced by § 12.3 ("Customer has made no ... minimum-volume ... commitment") with no residual volume floor elsewhere in the cited text.

elements.element: Customer pays only for usage or ordered Services.
elements.evidence: Rendered § 2.1: "...and pays only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form." This tracks § 7.1 ("Customer shall pay the Fees stated in each Order Form"; no unidentified "minimum-use ... charge"), so payment is tied solely to usage or ordered Services with no contradicting fee hook.

elements.element: The commitment is limited to the current 12-month term.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: rendered § 2.1 leaves no purchase or volume commitment of any duration, so there is nothing to confine to a 12-month term; the customer sits above the fallback rather than within it.

elements.element: Customer may reduce the commitment on 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: with no commitment created by § 2.1 (and § 12.3 confirming none exists), there is no quantum for Customer to reduce, which is strictly more favourable than a 30-day reduction right.

elements.element: Any shortfall is handled through a true-up rather than a penalty.
elements.evidence: Condition inapplicable: no minimum means no shortfall can arise, and the deleted penalty mechanic ("take-or-pay basis, without reduction or termination rights") is gone. The remaining "shortfall" language in §§ 22.2–22.3 relates to audited licence underpayments, not a volume floor.

reasons: Position-complete at the preferred level: rendered § 2.1 states both required propositions in operative language — no minimum purchase or volume commitment, and payment only for usage or Services ordered under an Order Form — with nothing left to a promise in the margin comment.
The fallback checklist is satisfied vacuously because the redline eliminates the commitment entirely; there is no term to cap, no quantum to reduce, and no shortfall to true up.

Minimal: only the single take-or-pay sentence in § 2.1 is replaced. Favourable existing language is retained untouched (§ 7.1 fee mechanics and the bar on unidentified minimum-use charges; § 12.3 no-minimum-volume acknowledgement), and no operative term is duplicated across sections — § 2.1 addresses the commitment, § 7.1 the payment mechanic.

Preserves intent: pricing, Order Form mechanics, fixed-fee/usage-based unit price allocation, timing, and remedies elsewhere are undisturbed, and the amendment removes rather than creates the internal conflict that existed between the old § 2.1 and § 12.3.

Claimed finding status of "deviation" is correct on the original: a multi-year take-or-pay expressly "without reduction or termination rights" is walk-away territory under MINCOMMIT, not merely short of the fallback, so a redline was required rather than a rationale note.

Comment is compliant in tone and content: it explains the change in two sentences, cites the playbook position, and offers the 12-month/30-day-notice/true-up fallback without lecturing. No further repair needed.
